### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**8** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **13** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 63db7240aae262a06fd61430fea84515c0928fa7` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `46854f677e8ff270032d92d890fd59c03697d52f` — the merge of head `5345c648fc9d7df25d4e7383594259394dff127c` into base `63db7240aae262a06fd61430fea84515c0928fa7`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 46854f677e8ff270032d92d890fd59c03697d52f && git checkout 46854f677e8ff270032d92d890fd59c03697d52f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 63db7240aae262a06fd61430fea84515c0928fa7 5345c648fc9d7df25d4e7383594259394dff127c && git checkout -B drift-repro 63db7240aae262a06fd61430fea84515c0928fa7 && git merge --no-ff 5345c648fc9d7df25d4e7383594259394dff127c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 63db7240aae262a06fd61430fea84515c0928fa7
```

Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/services/service-messaging/src/http-sender.ts, packages/services/service-messaging/src/memory-http-outbox.ts, packages/services/service-messaging/src/sql-http-outbox.ts, packages/services/service-messaging/src/http-sender-bodyless-33895.test.ts, packages/services/service-messaging/src/http-outbox.test.ts, packages/services/service-messaging/src/delivery-headers-at-rest.integration.test.ts, packages/services/service-messaging/src/http-outbox-parked-record.integration.test.ts, packages/services/service-messaging/src/http-signature-at-rest.integration.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-webhooks/src/webhook-drop-durable-record.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-webhooks/src/webhook-secret-at-rest.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-webhooks/src/webhook-signing-secret.test.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/http-nodes.ts + read, not reviewed: packages/services/service-messaging/src/index.ts, packages/services/service-messaging/src/http-dispatcher.ts, packages/services/service-messaging/src/messaging-service-plugin.ts, packages/services/service-messaging/src/http-outbox.ts, packages/core/src/security/http-signature.ts, packages/spec/src/automation/io-node-config.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/automation/webhook.zod.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-webhooks/src/auto-enqueuer.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-webhooks/src/sys-webhook.object.ts

Result in one line: this diff is NOT a narrowing. Plain `Clause-②: no` stands, the `(narrowing)` arm and everything it owes are not owed, and one should-fix (S1) is open on this head.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Durable `http` node, GET or HEAD — right.** `HttpConfigSchema` on `main` (`io-node-config.zod.ts`) takes any `method` string and routes `durable: true` through the outbox. Nothing an author can write changes. On `main` every such delivery died at `fetch`; here it delivers. That is a declared capability made real, not an accept-set change.
- **Signed bytes for GET/HEAD are the empty string — right.** `packages/core/src/security/http-signature.ts:11-12` publishes it: "A request with no body is signed over the empty string". Enqueue and send agree: both outboxes sign `deliveryBody(input.payload, input.method)` and store `input.method ?? 'POST'`; `sendOnce` resolves `delivery.method ?? 'POST'` the same way; the SQL row reads back `r.method ?? undefined`.
- **Default `Content-Type` omitted for a bodyless send — right.** An authored `Content-Type` header still goes out, because `delivery.headers` spreads after the defaults.
- **`FetchImpl` `init.body` becomes optional — right, and no arm.** The type is published (`index.ts:215`, reachable through `HttpDispatcherOptions.fetchImpl` and `sendHttpOnce`). An implementer that annotates `body: string`, or uses `init.body` as a string, gets a compile error after upgrading; nothing is refused at runtime. The seam is declared as "Override `globalThis.fetch` (tests)" (`http-dispatcher.ts:102`) and the dispatcher casts the global `fetch` to it. A function that cannot take a bodyless GET never could stand in for `fetch`, so the declared accept set is unchanged; `execution-duties.md` says pulling back to the declared contract does not touch Clause ②.
- **`httpDeliveryBody(payload, method?)` — right.** One optional parameter; every existing call returns the same bytes. `isBodylessMethod` is exported from `http-sender.ts` only, not from `index.ts`, so no name is added to the published entry.
- **Runtime move for a custom `fetchImpl` — not a capability taken away.** A GET/HEAD delivery that reached a custom implementation with `'{}'` and `Content-Type` now reaches it with neither. The only route there is a caller that builds `HttpDispatcher` or calls `sendHttpOnce` itself: `MessagingServicePlugin` (`messaging-service-plugin.ts:625-634`) passes no `fetchImpl` and exposes no option for one. No published text declares a GET that carries a body, and the product's own path refused every one.
- **Second producer, not named by the card or the PR — see S1.** `plugin-webhooks` enqueues with `method: sub.method` (`auto-enqueuer.ts:1247`, `:1404`), and `WebhookSchema.method` and the `sys_webhook` select both offer `GET`. A GET webhook moves from always dead to delivered with no body.
- **Seven recorder edits (`init.body ?? ''`) — right.** Every delivery those seven files enqueue is a POST, so no assertion is weakened.
- **`http-nodes.ts` comments — right.** Both reworded sentences match the code at this head.
- **Ablation heads — verified by blob id.** `http-sender.ts` is `c7f8fa4f` at `439f01b0` and at head; `sql-http-outbox.ts` (`b1ca5375`) and the new test file (`afff3bea`) are identical at `9c3d63d7` and at head.

### ② Semver level

- `patch` on `@objectstack/service-messaging` matches what the diff publishes. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: no spec file moves and no authorable key, value or default changes.
- Clause-②: `no`, with no arm, is the correct declaration. The `(narrowing)` arm is not owed, so neither are `!`, the BREAKING banner, an ADR-0087 marker, a `Skills-docs:` line or the dogfood battery. The changeset already carries the one-line migration for the type change ("now needs to accept `undefined` there").
- `@objectstack/plugin-webhooks`: test files only, no changeset owed.
- `@objectstack/service-automation`: its tarball ships `dist` only, the root `tsup.config.ts` drops `sourcesContent`, and `review-checklist.md` says map source text is not published. So the comment text does not ship. The second hunk adds two net lines, so the line mappings in `index.js.map` and `index.cjs.map` shift; the package's own CHANGELOG records an earlier comment-only change that measured exactly that and took a changeset. Not re-measured here. See N1.
- Check-runs on this head: 35 `success`, 16 `skipped`, none failed or pending. `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Lint & Repo Gates` and `TypeScript Type Check` are all `success`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev report 6898592135, open question (keep `no` with this review, or declare `(narrowing)`): answered, option A. See ① and ②.
- Dev report 6898592135 and 6897251215, out-of-scope finding "an authored body on a GET/HEAD durable node is dropped, carrier: none, noted, not filed": not accepted as filed-nowhere. This PR is the change that creates the drop. It is S1.
- Report 6897251215, the `http-nodes.ts` comment going stale: closed in this diff.
- Report 6897251215, rows at rest keep their old signature: carried by the changeset. Wording, N2.
- Deviation 1, recorder spelling `init.body ?? ''` instead of the amendment's `body?: string`: accepted (① above).
- Deviation 2, two comments reworded where the coordinator allowed one line: accepted; both made the same claim.
- `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:i18n`, NOT MEASURED locally by the dev: the head's lint and build check-runs are all green; I did not map those two families to a named check-run.
- Surface amendment 6897279605 says "no door's visible behaviour moves beyond that". The GET webhook move in ① is beyond the card's `http` node; S1 covers it.

### ④ Design judgment

Read against the published spec on `main`, the change delivers a capability the spec declares and the runtime did not deliver. It does not take one away at the consumer.

S1 (should-fix) — A GET or HEAD delivery now drops any payload and records `success`. For a durable `http` node with no body the dropped value is the placeholder `{}`, which is the card. Two other cases ride the same line and are not the placeholder:
  - an `http` node with `durable: true`, `method: 'GET'` and an authored `body`: the inline arm and the no-outbox fallback still fail loudly at `fetch`, while the outbox arm now reports success without the body;
  - every GET webhook: the whole event payload is dropped, the receiver gets headers only, and the `sys_http_delivery` row shows the stored payload next to `success`.
  On `main` both ended `dead` with `fetch`'s refusal as the row's error. `deliveryBody({ a: 1 }, 'GET') === ''` pins the drop as a unit, so it is deliberate, but the card, the claim's Responsibility line, the PR body and the changeset speak only of the `http` node with no body, and the dev left the flag with no carrier. Closing it takes one of:
  - fail loudly when a bodyless method carries a payload that is not the no-body value (the `http` node can tell at enqueue in `http-nodes.ts`, where `body` is still distinct from `{}`); or
  - an area or maintainer answer that the drop is the intended behaviour for both producers, written into the changeset, with a card for the GET webhook question (deliver with no body, or retire `GET` from `WebhookSchema`).

N1 (nit) — The changeset names `@objectstack/service-messaging` only, while the comment edit shifts the published `.map` files of `@objectstack/service-automation`. `review-checklist.md` asks the lane seat to check a changeset for every touched published package. The fix is on the prose face: add the package at `patch` with one "comments only, no behaviour change" sentence, or record the deviation at ACCEPT.

N2 (nit) — The changeset says rows at rest "were signed over `'{}'`". That holds for an `http` node with no body. A GET webhook row and a node with an authored body were signed over their own payload. Prose face.

N3 (nit) — The TSDoc on the published `FetchImpl` and `deliveryBody` links `isBodylessMethod`, which the package entry does not export. Prose face, or leave it.

No must-fix. S1 is open on this head and earns a delta review of its fix.

Delta round on record 6899205864 (head `4ed33935`). Result in one line: S1 is closed, N1 to N3 are closed, plain `Clause-②: no` still stands, and nothing graded above a nit is open on this head.

### ① Derived judgments

- **S1: closed.** A GET or HEAD delivery with a real body is no longer sent without it on any path.
  - Enqueue: `MemoryHttpOutbox.enqueue` and `SqlHttpOutbox.enqueue` call `assertBodylessPayloadAdmitted` after `assertEnqueueDeliverable` and before signing and the insert, so a refused input writes no row.
  - Send: `sendOnce` runs the same `bodylessPayloadRefusal` first and answers `retriable: false` without calling `fetch`. `classifyAttempt` turns that into `dead: true`, so a row that got in before this fix, or one reset by `redeliver`, ends `dead` with the refusal as its error.
  - No other writer of a `pending` row exists: `recordUndeliverable` writes `dead` on arrival and is never claimed.
- **Which payloads count as no body: right.** `undefined`, `null`, and an empty object whose prototype is `Object.prototype` or `null`. A string (the empty string included), an array, and any object with a key are refused. The SQL round trip keeps the answer the same at send: `undefined` is stored as `null`, `{}` comes back as `{}`.
- **The body-less durable `http` node still delivers: right.** `http-nodes.ts:394` enqueues `payload: body ?? {}`, which is admitted, sent with no body and signed over the empty string. The earlier delivery pins enqueue exactly `{}` and are green in CI.
- **Producer 1, the durable `http` node: right.** The enqueue sits in a `try`; a refusal returns `success: false` with `http (durable) failed to enqueue: ...`. On `main` the same node returned `success: true` with a `deliveryId` for a row that then died. The run now fails at that node, as the inline arm and the awaited no-outbox fallback already do when `fetch` refuses the same request.
- **Producer 2, the webhook auto-enqueuer: right, with N5.** `auto-enqueuer.ts:1241` and `:1398` call `void this.enqueue(...).then(ok, err)`; the reject arm is `reportWriteFailure`, so there is no unhandled rejection. Every webhook payload has keys, so every GET webhook event is refused.
- **Record save: not affected on either path.** The webhook enqueue is fire-and-forget off the event handler. A record-change flow runs inside `record-change-trigger.ts:340-379`, which catches and logs every flow failure and never fails the write.
- **No third producer.** `enqueueHttp` has two non-test callers in `packages/**/src`: the two above.
- **No new published name.** `bodylessPayloadRefusal` and `assertBodylessPayloadAdmitted` are exported from `http-sender.ts` only; `index.ts` is unchanged in this delta, so the package's `.d.ts` entry does not move.
- **Test file: right.** The two edited `deliveryBody` assertions now use the admitted shapes (`{}`, `undefined`); the new block pins four refusals, three admissions, a POST control, the send-time refusal and the sqlite refusal.

### ② Semver level

- Two `patch` changesets, one per package the diff moves. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: `HttpConfigSchema` and `WebhookSchema` parse exactly what they parsed, and no spec file is in the diff.
- Clause-②: plain `no` stands. The `(narrowing)` arm is not owed, so `!`, the BREAKING banner, an ADR-0087 marker, a `Skills-docs:` line and the dogfood battery are not owed either.
  - The area's reason does not hold, and is not the reason. `IHttpOutbox`, `EnqueueHttpInput`, `SqlHttpOutbox`, `MemoryHttpOutbox` and `MessagingService` are exported from the package entry (`index.ts:22`, `:169`, `:197-198`, the `.` export in `package.json`), `webhooks.mdx:477` names `messaging.enqueueHttp()`, and the 17.2 release notes treated an `IHttpOutbox.redeliver` signature change as caller-facing. `contract-review.md` reads the `exports` map as the published surface, so this door is published, not internal.
  - The reason it is still not a narrowing: the refused set is exactly the set the outbox's own transport already refused.
